title: Let's Keep Our Class Fish
passage_text:
Our class has a goldfish named Bubbles. Some people want to give him away. I think we should keep him.

Here are some facts. Bubbles lives in a tank by the window. Bubbles is three years old. He eats one pinch of food each morning. Taking care of him takes about five minutes a day. Our class made a chart, and every student gets a turn.

Now here is my opinion. Bubbles is the best part of our room. Watching him swim makes me feel calm. I think caring for him teaches us to be kind and careful.

Some people say a fish is too much work. But the facts show it is only a few minutes. Please vote to keep Bubbles!

skill_instances.quote: He eats one pinch of food each morning.
skill_instances.explanation: This is a fact. You can check it.

skill_instances.quote: Taking care of him takes about five minutes a day.
skill_instances.explanation: This is a fact. You can time it.

skill_instances.quote: Bubbles is the best part of our room.
skill_instances.explanation: This is an opinion. Not everyone may agree.

skill_instances.quote: Watching him swim makes me feel calm.
skill_instances.explanation: This is an opinion about a feeling.

skill_instances.quote: I think caring for him teaches us to be kind and careful.
skill_instances.explanation: I think tells us this is an opinion.

lesson_hooks.hook_question: How can you tell a fact from an opinion?
lesson_hooks.i_do: Model a fact first: 'He eats one pinch of food each morning.' It can be checked.
lesson_hooks.we_do: Students sort 'Bubbles is the best part of our room.' as fact or opinion.
lesson_hooks.you_do_question: Which sentence is a fact: 'Bubbles is three years old' or 'Bubbles is the best part of our room'?
